findings.title: CTF Flag Captured via SSRF + Local File Read (file:// Protocol)
findings.description: The Flask application exposes a profile_picture_url parameter that fetches URLs using Python's urllib.request.urlretrieve(), which supports the file:// protocol. This allowed reading arbitrary local files including the application source code (/app/app.py). The source code revealed: (1) hardcoded admin credentials (admin:adminpass), (2) Flask secret key ('supersecretkey'), (3) the flag displayed on the admin profile page. The /reset_password endpoint (localhost-only) was the intended exploit path via SSRF, but direct file:// access provided a shorter path to the flag.
findings.evidence:
FLAG: flag{335dd283-b8ce-4c22-b1d1-245c3f032575}

Exploit chain:
1. Register user 'attacker' at /register
2. Login and get session cookie
3. POST /profile with profile_picture_url=file:///app/app.py
4. File saved to /static/uploads/app.py, readable publicly
5. Source reveals admin:adminpass and flag value
6. Login as admin -> flag shown on profile page

Source code key lines:
  app.secret_key = 'supersecretkey'
  users = {'admin': {'password': 'adminpass', ...}}
  FLAG = 'flag{335dd283-b8ce-4c22-b1d1-245c3f032575}'
  urllib.request.urlretrieve(profile_picture_url, ...)  # no file:// filtering

reproduction.expected: Flask source code with hardcoded credentials and flag
